title: Using agents to build an agent company: Joao Moura

primary.label: Agent Architecture & Harnesses
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 77%).

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk centers on crewAI's multi-agent orchestration framework, covering agent anatomy, crews as multi-agent patterns, and production agent system architecture. crewAI is a developer framework for building agents, with demonstrated enterprise applications in marketing and lead qualification automation. The talk covers building crews locally, deploying them via crewAI Plus, and operating at production scale with 10M+ agent executions monthly. Prerequisites are basic LLM knowledge, but the content covers production agent architecture and enterprise deployment concepts. Recorded live at the AI Engineer World's Fair as a presentation by crewAI's founder. All evidence anchors are classified as 'said_in_transcript' grade, based on the speaker's claims during the presentation.

summary: João Moura opens with striking adoption metrics: over 10 million agents executed with crewAI in 30 days and 100,000 crews executed daily. He defines AI agents as LLMs capable of autonomous decision-making and tool use, contrasting them with traditional automation that requires explicit A-to-B connections. Agents adapt to circumstances in real time, enabling automations previously impossible. Moura describes agent anatomy—LLMs, tasks, tools, caching, memory, guard rails—and the added complexity when agents operate as crews with shared state, or when multiple crews interact. He frames this as a fundamental shift from strongly-typed software with predictable inputs and outputs to fuzzy AI systems where inputs and outputs are uncertain. Moura recounts crewAI's origin story: starting in Brazil, his wife encouraged him to share his LLM work online, so he built agents to automate LinkedIn posts. This succeeded, prompting him to build crewAI as a framework for more agents, during his anniversary trip. Early challenges included bugs, hallucinations, and errors, but community grew to 16,000+ GitHub stars and 8,000+ Discord members. He then built business crews: a marketing crew (content creator, social media analyst, senior writer, chief content officer) that achieved 10x more views in 16 days; a lead qualification crew (lead analyst, industry researcher, strategic planner) that generated 15+ customer calls in 2 weeks; and a code documentation crew that wrote crewAI's docs. Moura advises adopters to start simple and expand to low-risk, high-impact use cases. He announces new features: code execution via a single flag enabling agents to build their own tools; a 'train your crew' CLI that bakes instructions into agent memory for consistent results; universal platform support for third-party agents from LlamaIndex, LangChain, and AutoGen; and crewAI Plus, an enterprise offering that deploys crews as autoscaling APIs with bearer token auth and private VPC in three minutes, with one-click React component export. crewAI Plus includes a customizable demo UI, and the first 50 companies signing up receive access within 24 hours. Moura closes with a meta-demonstration: a crew that builds crews—given only an email and company name, it creates a crew, pushes it to a GitHub repository, and deploys it on crewAI Plus, eliminating the need to manually build a first crew. A 2-hour course is available at learn.crewai.com.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Opening Metrics and Agent Fundamentals
sections.summary: Moura opens with adoption stats (10M+ agents in 30 days, 100K crews daily) and defines AI agents as LLMs that can make autonomous decisions, use tools, and adapt in real time, contrasting with traditional A-to-B automation.

sections.title: Agent Anatomy and Software Paradigm Shift
sections.summary: Describes production agent complexity (caching, memory, guard rails, shared state across crews) and the shift from strongly-typed software with predictable inputs/outputs to fuzzy AI systems with uncertain inputs and black-box model outputs.

sections.title: crewAI Origin Story and Community Growth
sections.summary: Moura recounts starting crewAI in Brazil after his wife suggested sharing LLM work online; he built agents to automate LinkedIn posts, then crewAI during his anniversary. Despite early bugs, community grew to 16K+ GitHub stars and 8K+ Discord members.

sections.title: Building Business Crews: Marketing and Lead Qualification
sections.summary: Built a marketing crew (4 agents) achieving 10x views in 16 days, a lead qualification crew (3 agents) generating 15+ customer calls in 2 weeks, and a code documentation crew. Companies and investors including HubSpot's CTO and Jack Altman now back crewAI.

sections.title: New Feature Announcements
sections.summary: Announces code execution (single flag for agent-built tools), train-your-crew CLI for consistent results, universal platform support for third-party agents (LlamaIndex, LangChain, AutoGen), a new shipped version, and a 2-hour course at learn.crewai.com.

sections.title: crewAI Plus Enterprise Offering and Meta-Crew
sections.summary: Introduces crewAI Plus for enterprise: build crews locally, push to GitHub in three minutes to get autoscaling APIs with bearer token auth, private VPC, and one-click React component export. Includes a customizable demo UI. First 50 companies get access in under 24 hours. Closes with a meta-crew that builds crews from just an email and company name, creating and pushing a crew to GitHub for deployment on crewAI Plus.

demonstrations: Marketing crew with four agents (content creator specialist, social media analyst, senior content writer, chief content officer) checking X, LinkedIn, internet research, and past experience to produce content drafts

Lead qualification crew with three agents (lead analyst expert, industry researcher specialist, strategic planner) analyzing lead responses, comparing CRM data, and scoring leads with use cases and talking points
Code documentation crew that wrote crewAI's documentation autonomously

Meta-crew that builds crews: given an email and company name, it creates a crew, pushes it to a GitHub repository, ready for deployment on crewAI Plus
